name: Watch to Grow
manifesto: Two ways in: what you want them to grow, or a job you want them to see. Two thousand titles. Pick a door.

needs.name: Professions
needs.parent: I want my child to see what real jobs look like.
needs.promise: Movies and series as workplace field trips — what the job is, what it costs, what it is not.

needs.name: Curiosity
needs.parent: I want my child to become more curious.
needs.promise: The child leaves with a question they did not have before. Wonder is the point.

needs.name: World Knowledge
needs.parent: I want them to understand the world.
needs.promise: A real place, era, culture, or civic fact becomes discussable — a doorway, not a lecture.

needs.name: Resilience
needs.parent: I want them to become more resilient.
needs.promise: A character stays with a hard thing. Afterward you can name the skill, not just the plot.

needs.name: Creativity
needs.parent: I want them to think creatively.
needs.promise: Making, inventing, or seeing differently is the engine of the story — not decoration.

needs.name: Empathy
needs.parent: I want them to understand other people.
needs.promise: The child practices standing in someone else's shoes, including people who are hard to like.

needs.name: STEM
needs.parent: I want them to become interested in STEM.
needs.promise: Science, technology, engineering, or math drives the plot. Not a chalkboard cameo.

needs.name: Learn Through Stories
needs.parent: I want something educational but fun.
needs.promise: Fun first. Learning sneaks in. Use when tonight should not feel like homework.

ages.blurb: Shorter nights, gentler stakes, play after the credits.
Feelings, fairness, and first hard questions.
History, science, and social pressure with room to talk.
Heavier themes. Preview first. Still a conversation, not a lecture.
Workplace dramas and teen-plus themes. Preview an episode first.
Adult workplaces (finance, law, hospitals). Not a kids' night. Still useful as a career window if you watch with them.

howTo.headline: The parent is the user. The child is the learner. The film is the material.
howTo.lede: Watch to Grow is a lesson layer on top of movies you can already press play on. It is not a ranking of “best family films.”
howTo.note: If a card does not feel useful at your table, the page failed — not the child.

blocks.title: What a movie page contains
blocks.body: Recommended age, what kids may learn, qualities the story exercises, world knowledge, three conversation questions, one short activity, a parent note, and content notes worth previewing.

blocks.title: Professions
blocks.body: Use the Professions door when the question is “what is that job actually like?” A series can be a better workplace tour than a two-hour film. Adult shows (Billions, Boston Legal) are labeled 16+ on purpose — they are career windows, not bedtime.

blocks.title: What not to do
blocks.body: Do not turn the questions into a test. Do not skip the content notes because the rating looks mild. Do not hunt only for the “educational” scene — the learning is usually in how a character decides.

blocks.title: What Phase 1 is not
blocks.body: No accounts. No watchlists. No star ratings. No “three films for my 11-year-old who loves science.” That is later, and only if these cards earn it.

ritual: Age is a parent call. Content notes are honest.
The film is the material. You are the teacher.
Do not quiz. If they shrug, offer your answer and stop.
Keep it under 30 minutes, while the story is still warm.

professions.name: Lawyer
professions.look: Research, clients, negotiation, and court — not only closing arguments.

professions.name: Judge
professions.look: Procedure, discretion, and the gap between law and fairness.

professions.name: Investment analyst
professions.look: Reading companies, risk, and incentives — Billions is a warning label, not a how-to.

professions.name: Banker
professions.look: Capital, clients, and what gets sold as sophistication.

professions.name: Entrepreneur
professions.look: Building something from nothing, including the boring failure parts.

professions.name: Doctor
professions.look: Diagnosis, shifts, teamwork, and the limits of heroics.

professions.name: Nurse
professions.look: The work that actually keeps a hospital standing.

professions.name: Surgeon
professions.look: Training, precision, and responsibility when a body is on the table.

professions.name: Veterinarian
professions.look: Animal medicine plus the families who bring the animals in.

professions.name: Scientist
professions.look: Questions, experiments, dead ends, and publishing the result.

professions.name: Engineer
professions.look: Constraints, prototypes, and fixing what failed in public.

professions.name: Astronaut
professions.look: Training, systems, and teamwork more than blast-off.

professions.name: Programmer
professions.look: Building tools, debugging, and the ethics of what you ship.

professions.name: Teacher
professions.look: Planning, attention, and the politics of a classroom.

professions.name: Journalist
professions.look: Sources, facts, deadlines, and what not to invent.

professions.name: Chef
professions.look: Craft, hierarchy, pace, and taste as a serious skill.

professions.name: Architect
professions.look: Space, clients, and drawings that have to stand up.

professions.name: Pilot
professions.look: Checklists, weather, crew, and responsibility for other people.

professions.name: Firefighter
professions.look: Team drills, waiting, then minutes that matter.

professions.name: Detective
professions.look: Evidence, interviews, and patience — not a lone genius.

professions.name: Paramedic
professions.look: First hour medicine, calm under mess.

professions.name: Social worker
professions.look: Systems, families, and help that is not a speech.

professions.name: Diplomat
professions.look: Listening for countries, not winning an argument at dinner.

professions.name: Politician
professions.look: Public choice, compromise, and the cost of attention.

professions.name: Farmer
professions.look: Seasons, weather, money, and land as a job.

professions.name: Artist
professions.look: Practice, taste, and making a living from looking hard.

professions.name: Musician
professions.look: Rehearsal is the job. Performance is the visible sliver.

professions.name: Athlete
professions.look: Training, coaching, and a body as a workplace.

professions.name: Coach
professions.look: Teaching under scoreboards.

professions.name: Filmmaker
professions.look: Crews, shots, and finishing something other people will see.

professions.name: Writer
professions.look: Drafts, editors, and sitting with a sentence until it is true.

professions.name: Photographer
professions.look: Seeing, waiting, and choosing one frame.

professions.name: Designer
professions.look: Problems dressed as objects, apps, or clothes.

professions.name: Archaeologist
professions.look: Dirt, records, and patience with the past.

professions.name: Marine biologist
professions.look: Fieldwork plus the slow science under the pretty water.

professions.name: Environmentalist
professions.look: Measuring harm and arguing for a different default.

professions.name: Mechanic
professions.look: Diagnosis with tools. Machines as puzzles.

professions.name: Carpenter

professions.name: Psychologist
professions.look: Listening as skilled work, not advice-giving.

professions.name: Librarian

professions.name: Baker
professions.look: Time, temperature, and repetition.
